test_overview:
Evaluated the collaborative whiteboard app's Action History panel across 5 steps using Playwright browser automation with three browser contexts (context_A, context_B = separate board, context_C = second editor on board A). Server ran correctly on port 8000 throughout. Four of five steps passed fully; one step failed on a non-fatal verification.

Step 1 (PASS, 12/12): Board A created; blank-name submission kept the prompt open ('Please enter a name' placeholder) and drawing was blocked until 'Alex' was entered. Connected state shown; History panel accessible via button. Four content-changing actions (stroke, red stroke, one erase gesture, cleared board after confirm dialog) produced exactly 4 entries with correct action numbers, editor name 'Alex', and sensible descriptions. Tool/color switches created no entries.

Step 2 (PASS, 10/10): After explicit reload, returning editor 'Alex' skipped the name prompt and all 4 entries persisted. New board in fresh context enforced name entry ('Blake'); its history showed only its own 2 strokes with independent numbering (#1, #2), no cross-board leakage.

Step 3 (PASS, 12/12): context_C (new session, 'Casey') on board A required a name first, showed identical canvas and history. Drawing in A then C produced #5 (Alex) and #6 (Casey, blue) which propagated in near real-time to both panels without refresh, monotonic numbering, correct per-entry editor names, and consistent order.

Step 4 (FAIL, 0/10): Per-context offline in context_A correctly produced 'Reconnecting...' status, disabled toolbar, and blocked draw/erase/clear with no history entries and no changes visible in context_C - those non-fatal verifications passed. However, after restoring connectivity and drawing one stroke, context_C gained exactly one new entry (#7) while context_A rendered the entry TWICE (two '#7 Drew a stroke Alex' cards both flagged 'Latest'; internal history list also duplicated). The non-fatal verification 'only the post-reconnection stroke appears as a new history entry in both contexts' failed for context_A, so the step scored 0 per the non-fatal failure rule.

Step 5 (PASS, 8/8): 'Change name' to 'Alex2' updated identity, created no history entry itself, and the subsequent stroke was attributed to 'Alex2' while earlier entries remained 'Alex' (future-only attribution). The step's specific verifications passed; the pre-existing local duplication anomaly from step 4 persisted (two #8 cards locally) but is not part of this step's verifications - noted for continuity only.

Final score: 42/52.

steps.description: Step 1: test_history_panel_records_actions_with_metadata - PASS. Name enforcement verified (blank name rejected with 'Please enter a name' prompt, drawing blocked), 'Alex' accepted, Connected state, history panel accessible. Exactly 4 history entries (#1-#4) recorded with correct action numbers, editor 'Alex', and descriptions ('Drew a stroke', 'Drew a stroke' (red), 'Erased part of the board', 'Cleared the board' after confirm dialog). Tool/color switches created no entries. 12/12.

Step 2: test_history_persists_and_is_scoped_per_board - PASS. After reload, name prompt did not reappear for returning editor 'Alex' and all 4 history entries persisted. Fresh board in context_B enforced name entry ('Blake'); board B history contained only its own 2 strokes (#1, #2 by Blake) with independent numbering and no board-A actions. 10/10.

Step 3: test_history_syncs_in_realtime_across_editors - PASS. context_C ('Casey') required a name; both contexts showed same canvas and history. Actions drawn in A (#5 Alex) and C (#6 Casey, blue) appeared in near real-time in both history panels without refresh; monotonic numbering, correct per-entry editor names, consistent order. 12/12.

Step 4: test_history_not_recorded_while_disconnected - FAIL (non-fatal verification). Per-context offline produced 'Reconnecting...', disabled toolbar, and blocked draw/erase/clear with no history entries; context_C unchanged - these passed. But after reconnect, drawing one stroke produced exactly one #7 entry in context_C yet context_A duplicated the entry (two '#7 Drew a stroke Alex' cards both tagged 'Latest', confirmed stable). The verification 'only the post-reconnection stroke appears as a new history entry in both contexts' failed for context_A -> 0/10.

Step 5: test_change_name_affects_future_actions_only - PASS. Rename to 'Alex2' created no history entry; identity updated. Subsequent stroke attributed to 'Alex2' while all earlier entries still show 'Alex' (future-only name changes). Step verifications satisfied; pre-existing local duplication anomaly from step 4 noted but not part of this step's checks. 8/8.
